sections.body: This field covers the ways artificial intelligence is actually being used in research and teaching, not the imagined future. It includes tools that search and summarize published work, map citations, run statistical tests, code qualitative interviews, draft grant sections, check writing, design course materials, manage data, control lab instruments, and flag integrity problems. The work is practical and uneven. Some tools are mature enough to save time on literature searching and formatting, while others are still experimental or produce output that needs careful checking. The section describes what these systems do now, with their real limitations.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the work is mixed. Literature search and citation mapping are the most settled areas, with many tools able to find related papers and trace references quickly. Quantitative analysis has strong support for reproducible scripts and common statistical models, but automated interpretation can be wrong, and qualitative analysis tools can help with coding yet miss context and nuance. Grant writing and peer review tools can draft and critique text, but they do not understand a funder's priorities or a journal's unspoken standards. The site catalogues 732 AI tools and 801 scientific models, but a tool existing is not the same as a tool working well in a lab. Honest limits include hallucinated citations, shallow summaries, and the risk of treating a model's output as a finished analysis.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starting with Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis will learn how AI finds and summarizes studies, then move to Citation Mapping and Discovery to see how those studies connect. Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods cover the two main families of research methods, one for numbers and one for words. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review show how AI enters the writing and evaluation side of research. Course Design and Teaching shifts to the classroom, while Research Data and Repositories and Laboratory Automation and Simulation cover the physical and digital infrastructure of research. Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity sits across all of these, because every use of AI in research raises questions about authorship, data privacy, and honest reporting.
